artists.biography:
Crowded House are a pop rock band formed in Melbourne, Australia in 1985 by lead-vocalist and primary songwriter, New Zealand-born Neil Finn. Other members have included his brother Tim Finn, Australians Paul Hester, Nick Seymour and Peter Jones and Americans Mark Hart and Matt Sherrod.
Crowded House has won several national and international awards. In Australia, the group has won eleven ARIA Awards from 26 nominations, including the inaugural Best New Talent award in 1987. The majority of their ARIAs were awarded for their first two albums, Crowded House and Temple of Low Men. They won eight APRA Awards from eleven nominations and were nominated for The New Zealand Silver Scroll for "Don't Stop Now" in 2007.
"Don't Dream It's Over" was named the seventh best Australian song of all time in 2001.

perplexity.description:
Afterglow" is a compilation album by Crowded House, released in December 1999 by Capitol Records. The album gathers a collection of B-sides, outtakes, and rare tracks recorded between 1985 and 1994, offering fans a deeper look into the band's creative process during their most active years. Musically, "Afterglow" reflects the band's signature blend of melodic rock, jangly guitar textures, and introspective songwriting, with styles ranging from adult alternative pop/rock to college rock and indie influences. The tracks showcase the band's knack for crafting memorable hooks and thoughtful lyrics, even in material that didn't make their main studio albums.

In the context of Crowded House's discography, "Afterglow" serves as a companion piece to their core albums, highlighting lesser-known but often high-quality material that complements their official releases. While not a commercial blockbuster, the album was well-received by fans and critics for its consistency and the quality of its rarities. It stands as a testament to the band's enduring songwriting strength and remains a valued addition for collectors and longtime listeners of Crowded House's rock-oriented catalog.
